title: Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping
abstract: arXiv:2606.29983v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Looped Transformers, which repeatedly apply a shared transformer block, are an architecturally natural fit for variable-length algorithmic tasks. Although they can exhibit strong length generalization beyond the length of training sequences, this behavior is brittle, yielding high out-of-distribution (OOD) variance, even across well-performing in-distribution solutions. We trace this variance to the spurious correlation in simple algorithmic tasks between sequence length and number of loops. Introducing stochasticity into the number of loops during training sharply reduces OOD variance and stabilizes predictions across inference-time loop counts. To improve upon heuristic randomization schemes, we further analyze RL-Halting as a learned stochastic schedule and find that it generally improves the accuracy-stability trade-off. translated_title: 通过学习型随机停止方法稳定循环Transformer的外推能力
translated_abstract: 循环Transformer通过重复应用共享的Transformer块，在架构上天然适合可变长度的算法任务。尽管它们可以在超出训练序列长度时表现出很强的长度泛化能力，但这种行为是脆弱的，会产生较高的分布外（OOD）方差，即使在表现良好的分布内解决方案之间也是如此。我们将这种方差追溯到简单算法任务中序列长度与循环次数之间的虚假相关性。在训练过程中向循环次数引入随机性可以显著降低OOD方差，并使预测在各种推理时循环次数下保持稳定。为了改进启发式随机化方案，我们进一步将RL-Halting作为一种学习型随机调度进行分析，发现它通常能改善准确性与稳定性之间的权衡。在二进制加法、Dyck-1、Unique Set和Copy等任务上，学习型随机停止通常能改善这一权衡……
tldr: 该论文揭示了循环Transformer长度外推脆弱性的根源在于序列长度与循环次数之间的虚假相关性，并提出通过在训练中引入随机循环次数（包括学习型的RL-Halting调度）来显著降低分布外方差、稳定模型预测。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies the spurious correlation between sequence length and loop count as the root cause of brittle length extrapolation in looped transformers, and shows that introducing stochasticity into loop counts during training—including the learned RL-Halting schedule—sharply reduces OOD variance and stabilizes predictions.
